personas.label: Skeptical cleaner with low digital confidence
personas.background: A mid-40s worker in the commercial cleaning sector who has held part-time shifts for five years. They recently accepted a full-time offer from a services firm after a chaotic interview process.
personas.situation_now: Currently in the trial period of the new job but spends off-shift hours worrying if they missed hidden clauses in the offer letter they signed last month.
goals: Verify if the promised allowance is actually in the contract.
Understand if the new employer is legally bound by the verbal promises made during the offer call.
Keep this job stable to avoid the stress of searching again.
constraints: Only has 15-20 minutes of free time per day, usually late at night while waiting for public transport.
Uses an older, low-spec smartphone with slow internet, making long document loads frustrating.
Very low confidence in interpreting English legal text; expects to miss subtleties.
Skeptical of any automated tool, fearing it might 'steal' personal data.
personas.reading_style: Skims for bold text or numbers (salary, hours); skips paragraphs of fine print entirely unless explicitly told what to look for; trusts headlines over body text.
personas.attitude_to_ai: Distrustful; believes AI is 'too smart' and will probably give a generic 'correct' answer that ignores the specific context of their manual labor.
known_gaps: Does not know the difference between a 'fixed-term contract' and a 'permanent employee' status in Singapore.
Assumes 'probation' means they have no rights until it ends.
Unaware that an offer letter and a signed employment contract are different legal documents.
biases_or_habits: Relies more on advice from a union representative or a more experienced colleague than on written documents.
Tends to agree to things to avoid conflict, so may have accepted terms they didn't fully understand.
Will repeat actions (refreshing pages) rather than troubleshoot errors.
personas.voice: Direct and pragmatic, often using short sentences and practical examples (e.g., 'like when I used to clean the mall, the manager said X but paid Y').
personas.simulation_notes: Will likely abandon the task if it requires more than 3 screens of scrolling or if the interface looks complex. Needs very concrete, step-by-step guidance. Will ask for clarification if the AI sounds too formal or corporate. May give up if the system asks for login credentials or personal ID numbers.

personas.label: Veteran cleaning lead skeptical of digital check reports
personas.background: Ron has worked as a senior cleaning supervisor in commercial buildings for twenty years. He recently accepted a contract position with a new JLL competitor but is still finalizing his start date and training schedule. He prefers direct phone communication over any form of digital paperwork.
personas.situation_now: Ron is currently working his last week at his previous employer to cover shift gaps. He has printed the new offer letter but has not yet reviewed the 'digital check report' generated by the recruiting platform because he does not trust the automated summary.
goals: Ensure the start date aligns with his current employer's handover buffer.
Verify that the promised overtime allowance is explicitly written in the contract.
Avoid any clause that allows for unilateral change of shift schedule.
constraints: Only has 20 minutes between shifts to review documents.
Low comfort with scrolling through long digital PDFs; prefers printed text.
Distrusts automated AI summaries as 'computer guessing'.
High time pressure due to pending handover at old job.
personas.reading_style: Skims for bolded dates and dollar amounts; ignores paragraphs of legal text; will skip the 'detailed breakdown' section entirely.
personas.attitude_to_ai: Skeptical; assumes the report is biased or contains errors because 'machines don't understand union rules'.
known_gaps: Does not know how to verify the authenticity of the digital watermark on the report.
Unaware that 'discretionary bonus' is not guaranteed income.
biases_or_habits: Assumes if it isn't in the first paragraph, it's not important.
Tends to re-read the same sentence three times before moving on if it contains a complex word like 'indemnify'.
personas.voice: Blunt and pragmatic; uses short sentences and often ends with 'just tell me the bottom line.'
personas.simulation_notes: Will likely abandon the task if the interface requires hovering over elements or if the first screen is not clearly scannable. If the AI report contradicts the printed letter, he will assume the AI is wrong and stick to his printed copy.

personas.label: Experienced Operations Manager who skims for totals
personas.background: Rajan has spent 12 years in supply chain operations, currently mid-career and recently made redundant due to reorganization. He is a Singapore citizen with a stable family and no immediate financial crisis, but he is eager to return to work to maintain his career trajectory.
personas.situation_now: He received a full-time offer three months ago and signed it, but is now reviewing a new 'competitive counter-offer' from a different firm to decide if he should switch. He is currently in the final approval stage with the new company.
goals: Verify if the new offer's total compensation beats the current signed one
Confirm the role title justifies a 15% jump in salary
Ensure the start date is flexible enough to cover notice period
constraints: Only 15 minutes available before a family dinner
Low tolerance for verbose legal language
Assumes standard contract terms apply unless explicitly flagged
personas.reading_style: Skims headers and bolded numbers; jumps straight to the salary table and probation clause; ignores fine print in the middle sections
personas.attitude_to_ai: Skeptical; uses AI to summarize but trusts his own eyes for final numbers
known_gaps: Does not know the specific statutory implications of a 'conditional' offer in Singapore law
May miss a buried clause about a non-compete restriction in the appendix
biases_or_habits: Anchors heavily on the base salary figure, ignoring variable components
Skips sections labeled 'General Provisions' as irrelevant
Decides quickly based on the first number he sees
personas.voice: Direct, hurried, and focused on bottom-line figures.
personas.simulation_notes: Will likely skip the section on intellectual property rights entirely. If the check report flags a hidden penalty in the appendix, he may dismiss it as 'too complex to read now.' He will abandon the task if he feels the AI is asking him to read full paragraphs instead of giving bullet points.

personas.label: Tech-savvy IT Analyst with high caution
personas.background: Chloe has 4 years of experience in fintech IT support and is a PR holder in Singapore. She is currently unemployed after a 6-month gap and feels significant pressure to secure a role that allows her to continue her tech career path without demotion.
personas.situation_now: She accepted a junior role offer two months ago but has not started yet. She is currently reviewing a 'retention offer' from her previous employer, which is slightly lower in salary but offers better stability and no probation period.
goals: Identify any discrepancy between the verbal promise and the written offer
Verify the CPF contribution rate and leave entitlements explicitly
Ensure the job description matches the actual duties discussed in interviews
constraints: High anxiety about making the 'wrong' choice due to career gap
No time pressure from work, but mental energy is drained by job searching
High trust in written contracts over verbal assurances
personas.reading_style: Reads every word; highlights and copies text into a note-taking app; cross-references with online forums for specific clauses; checks for inconsistencies between sections
personas.attitude_to_ai: High trust; uses AI to draft questions for HR and to explain legal jargon in plain English
known_gaps: Uncertain about the practical enforcement of non-disclosure agreements in small firms
May overanalyze minor formatting errors as signs of unprofessionalism
Does not know the current market average for 'market adjustment' raises
biases_or_habits: Tends to assume the worst-case scenario for ambiguous terms
Re-reads the same section three times to confirm understanding
Seeks external validation for every red flag identified
personas.voice: Precise, cautious, and detail-oriented; often uses qualifiers like 'I think' or 'as written'.
personas.simulation_notes: Will spend significant time on the 'Red Flags' section. If the check report is vague, she will ask for specific line numbers or quotes. She is not impatient but may feel overwhelmed if the output is too dense; she prefers structured, categorized feedback. She will not skim; if the simulation forces brevity, she may complain that she missed details.
